title: News | Energy firm AEP plans $4 billion investment to power Google’s data center in Wyoming
key_facts: American Electric Power said on 14 Oct 2026 it will invest roughly $4 billion in a fuel-cell power plant near Cheyenne, Wyoming.
The 702-megawatt plant uses solid-oxide fuel-cell technology from Bloom Energy.
Google will buy the electricity under a 20-year power purchase agreement.
AEP will hold about 92% of Cheyenne Fuel Cell LLC; funds advised by Basalt Infrastructure Partners hold just under 8%.
Construction slated to begin in 2026, full commercial operation targeted by end of 2028.
AEP says it plans to add carbon capture as the project matures.
quote_evidence: American Electric Power said on October 14, 2026 that it will invest roughly $4 billion in a new fuel-cell power plant near Cheyenne, Wyoming, built to supply electricity to Google under a 20-year power purchase agreement.
Construction is slated to begin in 2026, with AEP and its partners targeting full commercial operation by the end of 2028.
why_it_matters_hint: A utility is building dedicated power for one tech customer.
notes: Secondary outlet; AEP release not seen.
